Prealgebra · Lesson 11.10

Families of Quadrilaterals

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Four-sided shapes are sorted into families by shared traits like parallel sides, equal sides, and right angles. Every member of a family has all of that family's properties, so once you know a shape is a parallelogram, every parallelogram rule applies to it. We start with a frame of four rods bolted loosely at the corners.

Problem
A picture frame is built from two 88 inch rods and two 55 inch rods, hinged loosely at the corners. Push on one corner and the rectangle leans into the slanted shape above, then leans further with another push. The angles keep changing. What is the perimeter of the leaning shape, in inches?
Show a hint
  • Leaning the frame does not change the rods, only the angles at the hinges.
  • Add up the four rod lengths, 8+5+8+58+5+8+5.
Show the full solution
Add up the four rod lengths. 8+5+8+5=268+5+8+5=26​ inches. Leaning the frame changes the angles at the hinges, never the rods, so every position has this same perimeter.
Problem
In one leaning position, the hinge at the bottom left of the frame reads 7070 degrees. The bottom rod and the top rod stay parallel, and so do the two side rods. Using what you know about parallel lines, how many degrees is the angle at the bottom right hinge?
Show a hint
  • The two side rods are parallel, and the bottom rod crosses both of them, so the two bottom angles are co-interior angles.
  • Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to 180180 degrees.
Show the full solution
The two bottom hinge angles add to 180180 degrees, so the right one is 180−70=110180−70=110​ degrees. The bottom rod crosses both parallel side rods, which is what makes those two angles co-interior.
Problem
A parallelogram-shaped stencil has a base of 1010 cm, slanted sides of 77 cm, and a height of 66 cm measured straight up from the base. Snip the overhanging triangle off one end and slide it across to plug the gap at the other end. The pieces form a rectangle. What is the stencil's area in square centimeters?
Show a hint
  • The rectangle you build has the same base and the same height as the stencil.
  • A 1010 by 66 rectangle has area 10×610×6.
Show the full solution
The rectangle is 1010 by 66, so the area is 10×6=6010×6=60​ square centimeters. The snipped triangle fills the gap exactly, so nothing is gained or lost, and the 77 cm slant never enters the calculation.
Problem
A solar panel shaped like a parallelogram has sides of 1212 m and 55 m. The perpendicular distance between its two 1212 m edges is 44 m. An installer multiplies 12×5=6012×5=60 and quotes the area as 6060 square meters. What is the actual area, in square meters?
Show a hint
  • Area needs the base times the height, and the height is the perpendicular distance, not the slanted side.
  • The base is 1212 and the height is 44.
Show the full solution
Area is base times height, 12×4=4812×4=48​ square meters. The 55 m side is slanted, so it is longer than the true height of 44 m, and using it overquotes by 1212 square meters.
Key idea
The parallelogram. A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel is a parallelogram. Opposite sides are equal, opposite angles are equal, and neighboring angles add to 180180 degrees, since each side is a transversal cutting two parallel lines. A parallelogram is defined by its parallel sides, not by its angles, so a hinged frame can tilt into infinitely many different parallelograms and still be one. Its area is base times height, b×hb×h. Cutting a triangle off one end and sliding it to the other turns any parallelogram into a rectangle with the same base and height. Measure the height perpendicular to the base. The slanted side is longer than the height unless the shape is a rectangle.
Problem
A club logo is drawn by marking a horizontal segment of length 1212 and a vertical segment of length 99 that cross at each other's midpoints, then connecting the four endpoints. The result is the rhombus above, a quadrilateral with four equal sides. It sits inside a dashed 1212 by 99 rectangle, and in each quarter of that rectangle the logo covers exactly half. What is the area of the logo?
Show a hint
  • The dashed rectangle has area 12×9=10812×9=108.
  • Each quarter-rectangle is cut along its diagonal, so the logo takes exactly half of the whole rectangle.
Show the full solution
The logo covers half the dashed rectangle, and 12×9=10812×9=108, so the area is 5454​. Each quarter of the rectangle is cut along its diagonal, which is why the logo takes exactly half.
Problem
A rhombus-shaped garden plot has an area of 4040 square feet. One diagonal measures 1010 feet. Using the pattern you just discovered, how many feet long is the other diagonal?
Show a hint
  • A rhombus fills half its bounding rectangle, so area == (diagonal ×× diagonal) ÷ 2÷2.
  • Solve 10×d÷2=4010×d÷2=40.
Show the full solution
The diagonals multiply to twice the area, 10×d=8010×d=80, so d=8d=8​ feet.
Problem
A highway warning sign is a rhombus with diagonals of 1212 inches and 1616 inches. The diagonals cross at right angles at their midpoints, cutting the sign into four identical right triangles. Use one of those triangles and the Pythagorean Theorem to find the side length of the sign, in inches.
Show a hint
  • Each right triangle has legs equal to half of each diagonal, 66 and 88.
  • Find the hypotenuse of a 66-88 right triangle.
Show the full solution
Half-diagonals of 66 and 88 form the legs, and the sign's side is the hypotenuse. Since 62+82=36+64=10062+82=36+64=100, the side is 100=10100​=10​ inches.
Key idea
The rhombus. A quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus. Its diagonals cross at right angles, cut each other in half, and split the rhombus into four matching right triangles. The area is half the product of the diagonals, 12d1d221​d1​d2​, because the rhombus fills exactly half of the rectangle its diagonals span. The side length comes from the two half-diagonals by the Pythagorean Theorem. Every rhombus is also a parallelogram, so base times height still works when you know a height.
Problem
A square napkin is folded once along its diagonal, and the crease measures 1010 inches. A square is a rhombus whose diagonals are equal, so both diagonals of the napkin are 1010. What is the napkin's area in square inches?
Show a hint
  • Use the rhombus area tool with d1=d2=10d1​=d2​=10.
  • Half of 10×1010×10.
Show the full solution
With equal diagonals of 1010, the rhombus tool gives 12×10×10=5021​×10×10=50​ square inches. You met this napkin in the last lesson, where the side came out to 1022​10​, and squaring that side gives the same 5050.
Key idea
How quadrilaterals are classified. Start with any quadrilateral. Give it one pair of parallel sides and it is a trapezoid. Make both pairs parallel and it is a parallelogram. From there, four right angles make a rectangle, four equal sides make a rhombus, and both together make a square. A type keeps every property of the types above it, so a square is a rectangle and a rhombus at once, and every rule in this lesson applies to it. Classification depends on properties, not on appearance.
Fun fact
Scissor lifts, folding gates, and camera tripods are built from rhombus linkages. Because a rhombus keeps opposite sides parallel at every angle of squeeze, the platform on top stays perfectly level while the whole structure stretches and collapses underneath it.
Problem
A kitchen backsplash uses trapezoid tiles with parallel edges of 55 inches and 1111 inches, set 44 inches apart. Tiles snap together in pairs, one flipped upside down as shown, forming a parallelogram. What is the area of that two-tile parallelogram, in square inches?
Show a hint
  • The flipped tile lays its 55 inch edge alongside the other tile's 1111 inch edge, so the parallelogram's base is 5+115+11.
  • Base 1616, height 44, area =16×4=16×4.
Show the full solution
Snapped together, the pair forms a parallelogram with base 5+11=165+11=16 and the same 44 inch height, so the area is 16×4=6416×4=64​ square inches.
Problem
One single tile is half of that two-tile parallelogram. Check the shortcut on a bigger tile. A trapezoid window has parallel edges of 99 feet and 1313 feet, set 66 feet apart. What is its area in square feet?
Show a hint
  • Two copies would form a parallelogram of base 9+13=229+13=22 and height 66, and the window is half of it.
  • Compute 12×22×621​×22×6.
Show the full solution
Doubling the window gives a parallelogram of area 22×6=13222×6=132, and one window is half of that, 12×132=6621​×132=66​ square feet. In one line, area =12(9+13)(6)=21​(9+13)(6).
Key idea
The trapezoid and its area formula. A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides. Those two sides are the bases. Two identical copies, one of them flipped, fit together into a parallelogram whose base is the sum of the two bases. So the area of a trapezoid is 12(b1+b2)×h21​(b1​+b2​)×h, which is the height times the average of the bases. Set the two bases equal and the formula becomes base times height, the rule for parallelograms, rectangles, and squares.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Here are four claims. (a) Every square is a rhombus. (b) Every rhombus is a square. (c) Every rectangle is a parallelogram. (d) A quadrilateral can have exactly three right angles. How many of the four claims are true?
Show the solution
(a) is true, a square's four equal sides make it a rhombus. (b) is false, a leaning rhombus has no right angles. (c) is true, right angles do not remove parallel sides. (d) is false, three right angles use up 270270 degrees and the fourth must be 9090, giving four right angles, never exactly three. That makes 22​ true claims.
Practice
One angle of a parallelogram measures 4848 degrees. How many degrees is the largest angle of the parallelogram?
Show the solution
A neighbor of the 4848 degree angle measures 180−48=132180−48=132 degrees, and opposite angles repeat the pair. The largest is 132132​.
Practice
A rhombus has a perimeter of 5252 cm, and one of its diagonals measures 2424 cm. Use the four right triangles inside the rhombus to find the length of the other diagonal, in centimeters.
Show the solution
Each side is 52÷4=1352÷4=13, and the half-diagonals are the legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse 1313. One leg is 24÷2=1224÷2=12, so the other satisfies a2+122=132a2+122=132, giving a2=169−144=25a2=169−144=25 and a=5a=5. The full diagonal is 2×5=102×5=10​ cm.
Practice
A stained-glass pane is a rhombus with diagonals of 1414 inches and 66 inches. What is its area in square inches?
Show the solution
Half the product of the diagonals is 12×14×6=4221​×14×6=42​ square inches.
Practice
A square coaster has a diagonal of 66 inches. What is its area in square inches?
Show the solution
Treat the square as a rhombus with equal diagonals. Its area is 12×6×6=1821​×6×6=18​ square inches, no side length needed.
Practice
A parallelogram-shaped field has an area of 9191 square meters and a base of 1313 meters. What is its height, in meters?
Show the solution
Height =91÷13=7=91÷13=7​ meters.
Practice
The cross-section of a drainage channel is a trapezoid with parallel edges of 44 feet and 1010 feet, set 55 feet apart. What is the area of the cross-section in square feet?
Show the solution
The average base is 4+102=724+10​=7, and 7×5=357×5=35​ square feet.
Practice
A trapezoid banner has an area of 6060 square inches, a height of 66 inches, and one base of 77 inches. How many inches long is the other base?
Show the solution
The sum of the bases is 2×606=2062×60​=20, so the other base is 20−7=1320−7=13​ inches.
Practice
A pixel-art gem on a screen has corners at (0,4)(0,4), (6,0)(6,0), (12,4)(12,4), and (6,8)(6,8). Its diagonals are the horizontal segment from (0,4)(0,4) to (12,4)(12,4) and the vertical segment from (6,0)(6,0) to (6,8)(6,8). What is the gem's area in square pixels?
Show the solution
The diagonals measure 1212 and 88, cross at (6,4)(6,4), and are perpendicular, so the area is 12×12×8=4821​×12×8=48​ square pixels.
Practice
A tile has four 66 cm sides and at least one right angle. Explain to yourself which family the tile must belong to, then find its area in square centimeters.
Show the solution
Four equal sides make the tile a rhombus, hence a parallelogram. One 9090 degree angle forces each neighbor to 180−90=90180−90=90, so all four angles are right and the tile is a square. Its area is 62=3662=36​ square centimeters.
